 Anthony Black, Desmond Bane, Franz Wagner, Jamal Cain and Wendell Carter Jr. will start Tuesday’s game against the Kings. 
 The Magic have made two changes to their starting lineup. Bane is back after missing Saturday’s loss to the Warriors, and Tristan da Silva (calf) being out opened up a spot for Orlando’s usual starting off-guard. The other change is Cain, whose insertion into the starting lineup comes at Jase Richardson’s expense. 
 Tristan da Silva 
 ORL 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Tristan da Silva (calf) is questionable for Tuesday’s game against the Kings. 
 da Silva popped up on the injury report Tuesday as questionable with a left calf strain. He’s potentially on the wrong side of questionable ahead of the matchup against the Kings. With Desmond Bane (illness) off the injury report, da Silva was likely to come off the bench anyway. 
 Desmond Bane 
 ORL 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Desmond Bane (illness) is not on the injury report for Tuesday’s game against the Kings. 
 Bane did not play in Saturday’s overtime loss to the Warriors, and Tristan da Silva started in his place. Bane’s return means that da Silva will come off the bench. 
 Desmond Bane 
 ORL 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Desmond Bane (illness) is out for Saturday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Bane wasn’t on the initial injury report, but has been ruled out Saturday with an illness. With Jalen Suggs and Paolo Banchero also out, Franz Wagner should have all the usage he can handle against the Warriors Saturday. 
 Tristan da Silva 
 ORL 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Tristan da Silva provided a boost off the bench with 18 points (6-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and four three-pointers against the Suns on Thursday. 
 All season long, da Silva has been a solid source of offense off the bench for Orlando, and he was able to provide that once again in this game. Unfortunately, he hasn’t been able to provide much outside of points and three-pointers, outside of a singular double-digit rebounding game last week. Aside from that night, da Silva hasn’t had more than four rebounds in a game. He’ll continue to score, but noting else will come consistently. 
 Tristan da Silva 
 ORL 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Tristan da Silva finished Sunday’s loss to the Celtics with 23 points (9-of-14 FGs), 10 rebounds, two assists and five three-pointers. 
 Injuries to Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) have not resulted in da Silva moving into the starting lineup. However, that doesn’t prevent him from providing reliable fantasy value. Against the Celtics, da Silva recorded his first double-double of the season and second of his NBA career. Rostered in 22 percent of Yahoo leagues, da Silva is a worthwhile pickup, even with the Magic playing three games next week. 
 Desmond Bane 
 ORL 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Desmond Bane accumulated 19 points (7-of-13 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics. 
 For the second straight game, Bane made at least five three-pointers, shooting 5-of-9 against the Celtics. The Magic guard shot over 50 percent from the field on Sunday, a sign he’s warming up after a slow start. Bane is shooting 36.9 percent from the field through six games, far below his career mark of 47.3 percent. Orlando begins a three-game Week 3 on Monday against the Wizards. 
 Desmond Bane 
 ORL 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Desmond Bane had 28 points (8-of-18 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, six assists, a block and six 3-pointers in 121-114 win against the Raptors. 
 After struggling against the Raptors on Wednesday, he played much better and hit 50% of his 3-pointers in this game. He hit all of his free throws and it was good to see him get back to where he was last season. Hopefully you didn’t panic if you had him. He won’t score 28 points every game but he will be much better than where he was. 
 Desmond Bane 
 ORL 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Desmond Bane put up 13 points (3-of-14 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, a steal, two blocks, and two 3-pointers in 99-129 loss to Raptors. 
 It was a bad night for Bane as he couldn’t get shots to fall against the Raptors. Bane in the past two seasons has shot 48.4% from the field, but he hasn’t shot very well this season. There is a good track record to indicate that there will be a bounce back from Bane and to not panic too much about his efficiency. He at least got you five rebounds and four assists to give you some value. 
 Tristan da Silva 
 ORL 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Tristan Da Silva with 20 points (8-of-10 FGs, 0-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, and four 3-pointers in 30 minutes off the bench against Raptors. 
 Anthony Black didn’t have it tonight, so Da Silva got some more extended run and did not disappoint. He’s not someone that is inherently a scorer, but he was hitting shots tonight when not many other people on the Magic were scoring against the Raptors. He’s a points and 3-point streamer if you’re looking for it in but he won’t shoot as efficiently as he did most nights.

 Payton Pritchard amassed 18 points (7-of-15 FGs), six rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the 76ers.
 After totaling 11 points in Boston’s first two games this month, Pritchard has scored in double figures in four straight games. Against the 76ers, the Celtics guard shot 4-of-8 from beyond the arc, the third straight game in which he’s made four three-pointers. Add in the rebounds and assists, and this was a good start to the week for Pritchard. He’ll look to extend his double-digit points streak to five when the Celtics visit the Raptors on Wednesday.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jayson Tatum

 Player Stats

 Jayson Tatum accounted for 21 points (8-of-17 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, two blocks and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the 76ers.
 Facing former teammate Jaylen Brown in a regular-season game for the first time since the latter was traded to the 76ers, Tatum outplayed Brown comfortably on Tuesday. The Celtics star came out sharp, scoring 11 first-quarter points on 4-of-7 shooting from the field. Tatum was relatively quiet the rest of the night, but he had plenty of help as four other Celtics finished in double figures, with Paul George’s 36 leading the way. The Celtics visit the Raptors on Wednesday, and Tatum was active for both games of Boston’s first two back-to-backs this season.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Paul George

 Paul George finished Tuesday’s win over the 76ers with 36 points (14-of-22 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, one assist and six three-pointers.
 On a night when most of the basketball world focused on Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown, George stole the show in his first regular-season game in Philadelphia since the offseason trade. After scoring 17 points in the first half, PG-13 dropped 14 in just over seven fourth-quarter minutes to help the Celtics put the game away. In his new home, George has remained healthy, and his production has been very good. It’s early, but he could be one of the steals of fantasy basketball this season.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 OG Anunoby finished Tuesday’s win over the Bucks with 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, two assists and five three-pointers.
 Anunoby entered Tuesday’s game shooting 29 percent from beyond the arc, so to say he needed a night like this would be accurate. The five triples are a new season-high for the Knicks forward, who did not record a steal or a blocked shot in a game for just the third time this season. Even with the slow start shooting the basketball, Anunoby’s skill set should allow him to reach his ADP (66), if not eventually surpass it.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Karl-Anthony Towns accumulated 21 points (5-of-14 FGs, 9-of-14 FTs), 16 rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Bucks.
 Towns didn’t shoot the ball well from the field or the foul line, but that didn’t eliminate all of his fantasy value. As has been the case all season, KAT was dominant on the glass, corralling a game-high 16 rebounds. Add in the assists and defensive contributions, and this was a good start to Towns’ four-game week. As a team, the Knicks outrebounded the Bucks 70-34, with Andre Drummond joining Towns in double figures with 14 rebounds.

 Jalen Brunson tallied 23 points (7-of-18 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one three-pointer in Tuesday’s win over the Bucks.
 Brunson didn’t have a great night shooting the basketball, but going 8-of-8 from the foul line gave the points tally a welcome boost. The good news for Brunson and the Knicks was that they were able to take care of the Bucks with relative ease, and the captain played just 28 minutes. The Knicks host the Cavaliers on Wednesday in what will be a far more challenging contest for the reigning NBA champs.

 Nate Ament recorded 10 points (4-of-8 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, two steals and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks.
 For the second time in as many games, Ament surpassed 20 minutes, playing 22 against the Knicks. The rookie’s stat line only lacked a blocked shot, and he shot 50 percent from the field. Unlike fellow Bucks rookie Brayden Burries (three points, three rebounds, three assists and one three-pointer), Ament’s chances to provide consistent fantasy value early in the season are unlikely to be there. That said, he’s someone who could be valuable to fantasy managers after the February trade deadline.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Ryan Rollins amassed 14 points (5-of-9 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks.
 The Bucks didn’t have Tyler Herro for Tuesday’s game, so Rollins made his first start since Halloween. While the production was solid, he logged 24 minutes, with Kasparas Jakučionis (11 points, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers) playing 23 minutes off the bench. If Herro remains out for Wednesday’s game against the Lakers, Rollins may still have some value in 12-team leagues. That said, his recent move to the bench and reduced minutes are a major concern for managers who selected Rollins with a middle-round pick.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 With Tyler Herro out with an injury, Jaquez led the Bucks starters in shot attempts and points Tuesday. Unfortunately, his efficiency suffered, especially in turnovers. Jaquez recorded a team-high four turnovers, the most he’s had in a game since racking up six in an October 23 loss to the Bulls. The good news is that Jaquez won’t have long to dwell on this performance, as the Bucks host the Lakers on Wednesday.
